isFallbackTitle rejects the lowercased titles "run command", "read file", "edit file", "write file", "search", "fetch", "tool", "agent", "file", "files", plus any bare tool name
Compact error string: "<Provider displayName> compacts its own context."
Start failure string: "<Provider displayName> did not start a session."
Refusal turn error: "The agent declined this request."
Close fallback error: "The agent exited."
Approval option roles map from ACP kinds: allow_always -> .approveAlways, reject_once and reject_always -> .decline, everything else -> .approve; an option's title falls back to its optionId
Approval kind mapping: command tool -> .command, edit tool -> .fileChange, everything else -> .tool
Search rows show the pattern as the title and the folder as the detail, only when the folder differs from the working directory and from the title
Read and edit rows show the relative path; command rows show ToolTitles.unwrapShell(rawInput.command)
Tool output is suppressed when it equals the literal "(no output)"
feature_notes: ACPLaunchGate spacing is 1.5 seconds; a lone start never waits because slot = max(now, nextSlot)
Cursor launch args: .auto -> ["--auto-review", "acp"], .fullAccess -> ["--force", "acp"], every other mode -> ["acp"]

Grok launch args: .supervised -> ["--permission-mode","default","agent","stdio"], .autoAcceptEdits -> ["--permission-mode","acceptEdits","agent","stdio"], .auto -> ["--permission-mode","auto","agent","stdio"], .fullAccess -> ["agent","--always-approve","stdio"]

Devin launch args (permission flag before the subcommand): .supervised -> ["--permission-mode","auto","acp"], .autoAcceptEdits -> ["--permission-mode","accept-edits","acp"], .auto -> ["--permission-mode","smart","acp"], .fullAccess -> ["--permission-mode","dangerous","acp"]; all other providers -> ["acp"]
JSONRPCConnection is constructed with sendsVersion: true

Auth retry: when opening the session throws an RPCError whose message case-insensitively contains "auth" and authMethods is non-empty, it calls authenticate with methodId = authMethods[0] and retries the open once

Resume: session/load is attempted only when configuration.resumeID exists and agentCapabilities.loadSession is true; isReplaying suppresses every session/update during the replay, and a failed load silently falls through to session/new
The client declares fs.readTextFile=false, fs.writeTextFile=false and terminal=false, so the agent never asks Droppy Code to do file or terminal I/O
Cursor-only _meta.parameterizedModelPicker = true unlocks the effort and Fast selectors; without it Cursor returns one baked-in variant per model and rejects other efforts
Images ride as prompt blocks {type:"image", mimeType, data} appended after the single text block
interrupt() answers every pending permission with outcome "cancelled", emits .requestResolved for each, clears the map, then notifies session/cancel

finishPrompt maps stopReason: cancelRequested or "cancelled" -> .interrupted; a thrown error -> .failed with error.localizedDescription; "refusal" -> .failed with "The agent declined this request."; otherwise .completed. It also clears todoToolCallIDs and cancels pending permissions
automaticOption answers permissions without prompting when runtimeMode is .fullAccess (any tool kind) or .autoAcceptEdits (only .edit), preferring an option of kind "allow_once" then "allow_always"
Mode resolution: planMode is the id exactly "plan"; buildMode is the first id among ["agent","build","code","default"], else the first id that is neither "plan" nor "ask"

orderedEfforts ranks none=0, minimal=1, low=2, medium=3, high=4, xhigh/extra-high/extra_high/"extra high"=5, max/ultra=6; it only reorders when more than one value is recognized, and unknown values keep their original index as the tiebreak (this fixes Grok advertising efforts from extra high down to low)
isEffortScale requires one of none, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, extra-high, which excludes Cursor's boolean `thinking` thought_level
baseModelID strips everything from the first "[" because Cursor's parameterized ids look like model[effort=high,...]
probeModelEfforts walks each model whose efforts are empty, makes it current via set_config_option to read back its thought_level scale, then restores the model the session started on when it differs

applyConfigOptions builds a Dictionary keyed by base model id for O(1) lookup, explicitly because OpenCode's roughly four hundred model walk replies four hundred times and a linear search per value stalled the main actor
A rebuilt model list preserves what earlier passes learned per model (efforts, defaultEffort, fastTier), because Cursor reports those for the current model only

Fast toggle: the config option whose category or id is "model_config" and whose id is exactly "fast"; applySelection writes the strings "true" and "false"; only the current model gets fastTier = "true", others get nil
applySelection prefers set_config_option and falls back to session/set_model, or to session/set_mode when hasModeAPI is true, when no config id was advertised
Message ids are "message-<messageId>" when the update carries messageId, otherwise a generated "message-<counter>-<first 8 UUID chars>"; thought ids use the "thought" prefix the same way
agent_message_chunk clears thoughtID; tool_call clears both messageID and thoughtID

usage_update reports occupancy only, as ContextUsage(usedTokens: used, windowTokens: size); the comment states it is deliberately never charged to the ledger because it measures the context window, not spend
session_info_update emits .title only for a non-empty title
current_mode_update emits .modeChanged(.plan) when the new mode equals planMode else .build, and only when planMode is known

Todo detection: rawInput.todos present, or a title in {todo, todos, todowrite, todo write, write todos}, or a title matching "<digits> todos" / "<digits> todo" (opencode's "3 todos"); such calls are routed to the checklist and never open a tool row, and later updates for the same id stay on the checklist
todoSteps looks in rawInput.todos, then rawOutput.todos, then content blocks of type "content" whose text parses as JSON, then rawOutput.output / rawOutput.stdout / rawOutput.text parsed as JSON

parseTodoItems accepts content, text, step or title for the label and skips whitespace-only entries; statuses completed|complete|done -> .done, in_progress|inProgress|in-progress|active -> .active, anything else -> .pending so an unknown provider state never drops an item
Tool kind mapping: "read" -> .read, "edit"/"delete"/"move" -> .edit, "search" -> .search, "execute" -> .command, "fetch" -> .web, default -> .other
Status mapping: "completed" -> .completed, "failed" -> .failed, anything else -> .running; an exitCode other than 0 downgrades a .completed update to .failed

pathKeys are searched in order: filePath, file_path, path, file, notebook_path, target_file, targetFile. Search patterns come from pattern, query, glob, regex, search. Web subjects come from url, query, prompt

subject() strips a leading phrase (longest first) from the list "searched web for ", "search web for ", "searching web for ", "searched the web for ", "search the web for ", "searched for ", "searching for ", "search for ", "reading file ", "read file ", "listed directory ", "listing directory ", "list directory ", "listed files in ", "list files in ", "listing files in " for .read/.edit/.search/.web kinds, then a single leading verb from the subjectVerbs set (read, reading, viewed, viewing, view, fetched, fetching, fetch, browsed, browsing, searched, searching, search, grep, glob, listed, listing, list, wrote, writing, write, edited, editing, edit, modified, modifying, modify, updated, updating, update, created, creating, create, deleted, deleting, delete, ran, running, run, executed, executing, execute, called, calling, call, opened, opening, open) and only when something remains, then unwraps a matching pair of ', ", curly quotes or backticks

isBareToolName returns an empty subject for read, write, edit, multiedit, patch, bash, shell, list, ls, glob, grep, search, webfetch, websearch, fetch, todowrite, todoread, task, tool, apply_patch, read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_files, search_files, run_command, run_terminal_cmd, web_search, web_fetch, codebase_search, file_search, grep_search, list_dir, view_file, replace_file_content
cleanTitle trims the character set "` \n" (backtick, space, newline) from both ends

makeToolUpdate refuses to let a bare tool-name title overwrite a real path, takes the path from locations[0].path for read and edit rows when no title arrived, and falls back to rawOutput.stdout/stderr/output joined by newline when no content blocks carry text
Diffs come from content blocks of type "diff" with path, oldText and newText; missing text defaults to the empty string
probeModels builds a catalog-only session in .supervised runtime mode and .build interaction mode, captures the .models event, runs probeModelEfforts and returns the list
handleClose fails an active prompt with the last lines of the process tail, then emits .exited unless stop() set isStopping
answerQuestion is an intentional empty no-op: ACP has no structured-question channel
The SessionConfiguration convenience init at the bottom of the file fills resumeID, resumeAt, model and effort with nil
unresolved_questions: The full list of ProviderKind cases routed through this class is not visible here: the doc comment names Cursor, OpenCode, Grok and Devin, but only cursor, grok and devin have explicit launchArguments branches, so the provider registry file must confirm which kinds instantiate ACPSession.
The exact shape of MCPProviderConfig.acpServers(allowsHTTP:) output and the `mcp-remote` fallback mentioned in the openSession comment are defined in another file.
How ModelOption.fastTier is rendered in the picker (beyond the literal "true" or nil written here) lives in the model picker UI, not this file.
JSONValue.compactString is not used here but String.nilIfEmpty is, and both are defined elsewhere; their exact semantics were not verifiable from this file.
configuration.fastMode and input.fastMode are read but TurnInput and SessionConfiguration are declared elsewhere, so their defaults are unknown from this file.

files.purpose: ProviderSession implementation for Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`) in headless newline-delimited stream-json mode: builds the launch flags, streams init/step_update/result events into Droppy events, snapshots files around edit steps to synthesize diffs, tracks per-turn token spend, and supplies the static model catalog, auth-status probe and plan-limit readers for /usage and /credits.

side_effects: Launches the `agy` CLI as a long-lived child process with stream-json stdio and the thread's folder passed through --add-dir
Writes one JSON object per turn on the child's stdin: {"event":"user","message":{"content":"<text>"}}
Reads the child's message stream in a detached Task until it ends, then calls didClose()
Terminates the child process on interrupt(), stop() and the start timeout
Reads files off disk (snapshot) before and after an edit step to build the diff
Runs one-off shell commands: `agy models`, `agy -p /model --output-format json`, `agy -p /usage --output-format json`, `agy -p /credits --output-format json`
A 30-second start watchdog Task that terminates the process and fails start
Emits a .notice warning when a result reports denied_actions
platform_assumptions: Swift concurrency with @MainActor isolation and CheckedContinuation for the start handshake
Unix child-process stdio pipes (StdioProcess) and an `agy` binary resolvable as a URL executable
URL(fileURLWithPath:) plus resourceValues(forKeys: [.fileSizeKey]) for the 1 MB snapshot guard, and String(contentsOf:encoding: .utf8)
Antigravity's own scratch location ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch is the cwd fallback when --add-dir is absent (the documented reason for passing the flag)
Google sign-in cached by the `agy` CLI, or a GEMINI_API_KEY environment variable, as the auth source

Header states the protocol was verified live against agy 1.2.2 (models TSV, /usage and /credits headless envelopes, tool step shapes, denied_actions), reference https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/headless/
persisted_fields: No app preferences are written here. Inbound event names and fields: `init` with conversation_id; `step_update` with step_update.step_index, step_type "agent_response" or "tool", text_delta, usage.input_tokens, usage.cache_read_tokens, usage.output_tokens, tool_name, tool_info.name, tool_info.parameters, tool_info.error.message, tool_info.output, state "ACTIVE"/"DONE"/"ERROR"; `result` with result.usage.total_tokens, result.usage.input_tokens, result.usage.output_tokens, result.response, result.denied_actions[].display_name and .action, result.conversation_id, result.status, result.error
/usage JSON envelope: command.data.groups[].name, groups[].buckets[].{id, name, remaining_fraction, reset_time}, with a top-level `response` text fallback
/credits JSON envelope: command.data.remaining_credits (Int), with a `response` text fallback
/model JSON envelope: command.data.id as the current model id

Tool parameter display keys read from the stream: AbsolutePath, TargetFile, NotebookPath, FilePath, File, file, path, Path, DirectoryPath, directory, dir, CommandLine, command, Command, Url, URL, url, Query, query, Pattern, pattern, SearchPath, SearchDirectory, Task, task, Prompt, prompt, Description, description, ServerName, server_name, Server, server, ToolName, tool_name, Tool, tool, Arguments, arguments, Input, StartLine, EndLine
PlanLimits.Window ids produced: the bucket's own `id` or "<groupName>-<windowCount>", "usage-<index>" for the text fallback, and the literal "ai-credits" for the credit window
ui_elements: Start timeout message: "Antigravity did not answer. Is `agy` signed in? Run `agy` once in Terminal."
Compact message: "Antigravity manages its own context."
Auth hint: "Antigravity is not signed in. Run `agy` once in Terminal to sign in."
Process-exit fallbacks: "Antigravity exited." and the turn failure default "Antigravity stopped before finishing."
Denied-actions warning notice: "Antigravity held back <names> without prompting. Use Full access or add an allow rule in the CLI's settings." with names joined by ", "
WAITING-with-denials turn error: "Antigravity held back <names> waiting for a permission it could not ask for. Use Full access for this chat."
Generic tool failure output when no error message is present: "The tool failed."
Catalog errors: "`agy models` produced no output." and "`agy models` listed no models."
MCP tool row title formatted as "<server> · <tool>" with a middle dot, defaulting to "MCP" and "tool"
Plan-limit window titles "<group> · <bucket name>" (default bucket name "Limit", default group name "Models") and "AI credits · <n> remaining"
Read-row detail line-range strings "L<start>–<end>" using an en dash, or "L<start>" when no larger end line is given
Agent tool row title truncated with TextCleanup.singleLine(..., limit: 96)
Other-kind tool detail is shown only when it is non-empty, is not "{}" and is at most 300 characters
feature_notes: Fixed launch flags, in order: --input-format stream-json, --output-format stream-json, --print-timeout 30m, --add-dir <workingDirectory>
Connected MCP servers are passed as --allowed-mcp-server-names followed by every id from MCPProviderConfig.connectedIDs(), so the user's other servers stay out of the session without being touched
--model and --effort are appended only when normalize() returns non-empty values; --conversation <resumeID> is appended when a non-empty resumeID exists

modeArguments: interaction .plan produces ["--mode","plan"]; otherwise .supervised adds nothing while .autoAcceptEdits, .auto and .fullAccess add ["--mode","accept-edits"]; .fullAccess additionally appends --dangerously-skip-permissions
start() awaits a CheckedContinuation resolved by the init event's conversation_id, guarded by a 30-second Task.sleep watchdog that terminates the process and throws the timeout message
Images are never sent: stream-json accepts text blocks only, and anything else ends the session with an error

interrupt() sets isStopping = true before terminating so didClose reports .interrupted instead of the chat reading "Antigravity stopped unexpectedly"; start() clears the flag again for the next launch. The stream has no interrupt request, and the conversation persists server-side for the next --conversation resume
resolveApproval and answerQuestion are deliberate no-ops because headless runs cannot be prompted
Step ids are namespaced per launch: "agy-<launchID>-message-<step_index>", "agy-<launchID>-tool-<step_index>", and result-only replies use "agy-<launchID>-result-<first 8 UUID chars>"
agent_response steps feed the context meter from usage and stream text_delta; empty text is ignored and does not set streamedText
Tool steps: the first sighting inserts the id into startedTools and emits .toolStarted; when state is "ACTIVE" it returns there, and an edit-kind call snapshots the file first
Failure detection: state == "ERROR", or state == "DONE" with tool_info.error.message present; a denied message becomes ToolCall.Status.declined rather than .failed
isDenied matches lowercased text containing "permission check failed", "denied permission" or "permission denied"
finishEdit returns [FileEdit(path:)] with no diff when the file is unchanged and [FileEdit(path:old:new:)] otherwise; nil for non-edit steps so the update leaves existing edits alone
snapshot() reads UTF-8 text files of at most 1,000,000 bytes; anything larger, binary or missing reads as empty so a write shows as a whole-file addition
Per-step context usage = input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + output_tokens with windowTokens nil, emitted only when the sum is greater than 0

Result token totals are cumulative over the session, so spendTracker.spend(total:) converts them to a per-turn delta; only a positive delta is recorded to TokenLedger.shared and emitted as .tokenSpend(TokenSpend(provider: .antigravity, totalTokens: spend, model: model))
A resumed conversation starts with spendBaselineKnown = false, so the first total seeds the baseline via seedBaseline(total:) and is never charged as spend nor reported as zero
used falls back to input_tokens + output_tokens when total_tokens is absent
handleResult clears editSnapshots and startedTools and sets turnActive = false before anything else

Result status mapping: "WAITING" with denied actions -> .failed with the held-back message; "SUCCESS" or plain "WAITING" -> .completed (WAITING means the agent stopped to ask something it cannot ask headless); "CANCELED" or "INTERRUPTED" -> .interrupted; anything else -> .failed with result.error when non-empty, else "Antigravity stopped before finishing."; interruptRequested overrides all of this with .interrupted
A turn whose reply never streamed replays result.response as .messageCompleted, so resumed conversations still show their text
A non-empty result.conversation_id re-emits .sessionReady before the status is handled
authHint fires on a tail containing "authentication required", "not signed in", "unauthenticated", or both "login" and "agy"
parseModelRow strips the suffixes -high, -medium, -low (checked in that order) from the slug and the matching " (High)", " (Medium)" or " (Low)" suffix from the display name

normalize(): an empty model returns (nil, nil); a base slug containing "claude" gets no effort at all (Claude models hosted on Antigravity do not take --effort); otherwise the effort falls back to the slug's own suffix, then to "medium" for gpt-oss-120b and "high" for everything else; gemini-3.1-pro rejects "medium" and is bumped to "high"; gpt-oss-120b is always forced to "medium"

listModels runs `agy models` and `agy -p /model --output-format json` concurrently with 30-second timeouts, strips ANSI, parses tab-separated slug/name rows (name falls back to the slug), collapses effort variants into one base entry and orders efforts as low, medium, high with defaultEffort "high" when present else the last available

A model is the default when its slug equals command.data.id, its base slug equals it, or the current id has the base slug as a prefix; if nothing matched, the first entry is rewritten with isDefault: true
isSlug requires a leading letter or digit and only letters, digits, hyphen, underscore and dot, with no spaces; progress output goes to stderr so only stdout rows are parsed

authStatus runs `agy models` with a 20-second timeout: success plus at least one slug row -> .signedIn(nil); otherwise combined stdout+stderr containing "authentication required", "not signed in", "unauthenticated", "sign in" or "login" -> .signedOut; a bare success -> .signedIn(nil); anything else -> .unknown. It never spends tokens

readPlanLimits runs /usage and /credits concurrently with 30-second timeouts, both described as zero-token headless calls, returns nil when no windows parsed and otherwise PlanLimits(planName: nil, windows: windows)

Usage percent = max(0, min(100, (1 - remaining_fraction) * 100)); the older tab-separated text fallback uses 100 - remaining where remaining is the third column with "%" stripped, and the optional fourth column is an ISO 8601 reset date

The credits window percent is 0 while remaining_credits is greater than 0 and 100 when it reaches zero, with no reset time; the text fallback looks for a row whose first column contains "credit" and whose second column parses as an Int

Tool kind table, exact tool names: command = run_command, send_command_input, command_status, wait, wait_5_seconds, schedule; read = view_file, view_file_outline, view_code_item, view_content_chunk, read_resource, read_browser_page, capture_browser_screenshot, capture_browser_console_logs; edit = write_to_file, replace_file_content, multi_replace_file_content, sed_file, notebook_edit, notebook_execution; search = list_dir, grep_search, find_by_name, list_resources, list_browser_pages; web = search_web, read_url_content, open_browser_url, browser_click_element, browser_drag_pixel_to_pixel, browser_get_dom, browser_get_network_request, browser_input, browser_list_network_requests, browser_mouse_down, browser_mouse_up, browser_move_mouse, browser_press_key, browser_refresh_page, browser_resize_window, browser_scroll, browser_scroll_dom, browser_select_option, click_browser_pixel, execute_browser_javascript; agent = invoke_subagent, browser_subagent, define_subagent, manage_subagents; mcp = call_mcp_tool; everything else falls to other
Read rows fall back to a Url/URL/url parameter when no path is present, and add the line range as the detail only when a path was found
Edit rows attach [FileEdit(path:)] at start time so the row names its file before the diff exists
Search rows title on the pattern with the folder as detail, or fall back to the folder alone, then to the humanized tool name
humanize capitalizes only the first underscore-separated word and joins the rest with spaces, so run_command becomes "Run command"
user_input acknowledgements and checkpoint markers in the stream are deliberately ignored because Droppy Code renders nothing for them
unresolved_questions: TokenSpendTracker's delta algorithm (in particular how it handles a cumulative total that goes backwards) is defined in another file, so the exact per-turn spend arithmetic is not fully visible from here.
The supportsImages gate that stops images reaching this session is referenced in a comment but lives in the provider capability table, not this file.
Whether the step `state` vocabulary has values beyond ACTIVE, DONE and ERROR is unknown: any other state simply produces no update after the start event.
How `--print-timeout 30m` interacts with the 30-second start watchdog is not stated in this file.
